intended_object: The canonical isomorphism (A ⊗_ℤ O(GLₙ)) / J_A ≅ A ⊗_ℤ (O(GLₙ)/J) of commutative Hopf A-algebras. Here J is the Hopf ideal that cuts out the Chevalley group scheme generated by the Kostant root subgroups inside GLₙ over ℤ, and J_A is its base change along ℤ → A. In words: base change commutes with the presentation as a closed subgroup scheme. I took this from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body applies the library's general isomorphism `CommHopfAlgCat.quotientBaseChangeIso` to the specific defining ideal `kostantGeneratedDefiningIdeal`. That general isomorphism holds for any Hopf ideal J of a commutative Hopf k-algebra H and any base change k → K. It is built as `quotientKerOfSurjectiveIso` from the base change of the quotient map H → H/J. That base-changed map is surjective, and its kernel is the base-changed ideal J_K, i.e. the image of K ⊗ J (right exactness of the tensor product). So the result is the canonical map induced by id_K ⊗ (H → H/J), which is the standard identification. The companion simp lemma `mkQuotient_comp_kostantGeneratedBaseChangeIso_hom` confirms it is compatible with the quotient maps.

Both sides of the stated type match the docstring: the left is the quotient of the base-changed GLₙ coordinate algebra by the base-changed ideal, and the right is the base change of the carrier over ℤ.

The definition is a specialization of a general isomorphism, but it names the canonical isomorphism for one particular group scheme. Being specific to that object does not make it too narrow, since the general version is already in the library. The ℤ-base and the GLₙ setting are part of the content of the Chevalley-carrier construction. Mathlib has no Hopf-ideal quotients or this base-change isomorphism, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
